Melbourne.text: Victoria's capital first overtook Sydney as Australia's biggest city in 1865; on this count it is ahead again.
Melbourne.evidence: Exponential growth ensued, and by 1865, Melbourne had overtaken Sydney as Australia's most populous city.

Sydney.text: The capital of New South Wales has seventy surf beaches, Bondi the most famous.
Sydney.evidence: Seventy surf beaches can be found along its coastline, with Bondi Beach being the most famous.

Brisbane.text: Queensland's capital will host the 2032 Summer Olympics. It also bid for 1992, and lost to Barcelona.
Brisbane.evidence: It will host the 2032 Summer Olympics and 2032 Summer Paralympics in Victoria Park. The city also bid for the 1992 Summer Olympics but lost to Barcelona.

Perth.text: Western Australia's capital is one of the most isolated big cities in the world.
Perth.evidence: With more than two million residents, Perth is one of the most isolated major cities in the world.

Adelaide.text: South Australia's capital was built for free settlers, not convicts: its 1837 plan had no prison.
Adelaide.evidence: Adelaide was established as a planned colony of free settlers ... As it was believed that in a colony of free settlers there would be little crime, no provision was made for a gaol (Prison) in Colonel Light's 1837 plan.

Gold Coast.text: In 2007 this Queensland city passed Newcastle to become Australia's largest city that isn't a capital.
Gold Coast.evidence: In 2007, the Gold Coast overtook the population of Newcastle, New South Wales, to become the sixth largest city in Australia and the largest non-capital city.

Newcastle.text: This New South Wales city is the world's largest coal-exporting harbour: 143 million tonnes in 2022.
Newcastle.evidence: Famous for its coal, Newcastle is the largest coal exporting harbour in the world, exporting 143 million tonnes of coal in 2022.

Canberra.text: Built in the Australian Capital Territory as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne, it was designed by two architects from Chicago.
Canberra.evidence: being a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne, Australia's two largest cities. ... the design by Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin of Chicago, Illinois, United States, being declared the winner.

Sunshine Coast.text: James Cook saw its Glass House Mountains, in Queensland, from the Endeavour in 1770.
Sunshine Coast.evidence: In 1770, James Cook on the deck of HMS Bark Endeavour became the first known European to sight the Glass House Mountains, located south-west of Caloundra.

Central Coast.text: This New South Wales region is why Greater Sydney still outnumbers Greater Melbourne: the ABS counts it as part of Sydney.
Central Coast.evidence: ABS currently includes the Central Coast region population wholly within Greater Sydney which results in Greater Sydney's population being larger than that of Greater Melbourne.
